title: Train rotation + hotpatch roundup
content:
Meeting: Train rotation + hotpatch roundup
Date: 2026-03-10 14:00 UTC
Location: Zoom / #release-ops Slack thread (see linked_artifacts)
Facilitator: Marcus Chen
Note: informal; capturing rough decisions, open questions, and action items for follow-up.

Attendees:
- Marcus Chen (release-engineering)
- Lina Gomez (serving-runtime)
- Tom Rivers (platform infra)
- Priya Nair (console & rollouts)
- Ethan Park (SRE)
- Ruth Alvarez (product-hosted-api)
- Observers: 2 PM mobile team engineers (brief attendance)

Agenda:
1) Quick sync on current release train (v2026.03) status
2) Hotpatches since last train and RCA summary
3) Change log bundling / artifact promotion cadence
4) Canary ramp adjustments & rollback criteria refinement
5) Open concerns, action items, next train date

1) Release train status (v2026.03)
- Cut branch: release/2026.03 queued at 03/09 22:30 UTC.
- Blockers: 1 flaky e2e test in model-serving suite (TEST-ml-serve-flaky, flaky on seq-length>2048). Working hypothesis: new attention kernel regression on CUDA 12.2 builds.
- Throughput target: 350 qps sustained for 8xA10s pool; currently at 320 qps in load tests (10% under target).
- Canary plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 4h windows. First canary scheduled 03/11 02:00 UTC maintenance window.

Notes: Lina will re-run load tests with quantized build (int8) to see if throughput gap closes. If not resolved, consider temporary auto-scale policy bump for Dedicated pools.

2) Hotpatch summary (hotpatches since 2026-03-01)
- Hotpatch HP-2026-03-05-A: Fix for tokenization edge-case causing 502s on long instruction prompts. Deployed 03/05 04:15 UTC, rollback not required. Root cause: incomplete fallback in tokenizer merge logic. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1287. Owner: Priya.
- Hotpatch HP-2026-03-08-B: Emergency memory leak fix (kv-cache) in attention cache clear code. Deployed 03/08 19:40 UTC. Impact: prevented two Dedicated clusters from OOM; triggered one P1 page during peak but recovered. Owner: Tom.
- Post-deploy RCA notes: both hotpatches were cherry-picked onto release branch but not included in initial changelog bundle (gap in release tooling). Action: ensure hotpatch tags are auto-appended to next changelog.

3) Change log bundling / artifact promotion
Problem observed: manual tagging step allowed hotpatch churn to be omitted from customer-facing changelog (reported by CS). Customers saw behavior differences between Hosted API and release notes.
Decision: adopt an automated small-footprint strategy for hotpatches:
- Any hotpatch merged to main/deploy must include a CHANGES entry (short, 1-line) in /docs/changes/hotpatches/ with PR id.
- Release pipeline will scan hotpatch dir and auto-merge entries into the next train's changelog during artifact promotion.
Owner: Marcus to file automation ticket (REL-491).

4) Canary ramp & rollback criteria (refinement)
Current canary ramp: 5/20/50/100 with health checks: 2xx rate > 99.5%, 95th latency < 1.2x baseline, error budget burn < 0.1%/hour.
Proposed refinement: add model-quality signal (prompt-eval synthetic corpus) to canary gating for Hosted API customers:
- Evaluate 50 deterministic prompts (representative set) during each canary step. Threshold: mean log-loss delta < 0.02 relative to baseline.
- If model-quality or latency thresholds fail at any step, immediate rollback to previous artifact and open rollback incident (REL-ROLL-<timestamp>).

Decision: adopt model-quality gating for canary steps starting v2026.04; experimental pilot for this train to monitor feasibility (we will not block rollout for v2026.03 but will collect metrics).
Owner: Lina to wire up synthetic prompt harness in CI (ticket ENG-3221).

5) Risks and open concerns
- CUDA kernel regression risk: if upstream CUDA 12.2 builds keep failing, we may need to pin certain nodes to previous drivers; this impacts Dedicated capacity and customers pinned to builds.
- Changelog communication gap: CS wants a pre-release notification for enterprise customers whenever a hotpatch touches authentication, billing, or model semantics.
- Weekend maintenance window: 03/13 02:00-06:00 UTC might coincide with customer deployments in APAC. Need to notify early and provide a pre-warning banner.

Action items (owner — due):
- Lina Gomez — re-run throughput tests with int8 quantized build and post detailed results to #release-ops (due 2026-03-11 by 10:00 UTC).
- Marcus Chen — create automation ticket REL-491 to merge hotpatch CHANGES into release changelog; include POC script (due 2026-03-12).
- Priya Nair — add CHANGES entry for HP-2026-03-05-A and confirm that PR link is included in next changelog bundle (due 2026-03-11).
- Tom Rivers — push KV-cache memory leak follow-up patch to main (PR + unit tests) and update rollback steps doc (due 2026-03-14).
- Ethan Park — update SRE runbook with new model-quality canary gating and rollback incident naming convention (due 2026-03-15).
- Ruth Alvarez/CS — prepare customer email draft for pre-release notification about maintenance window and hotpatch semantics (due 2026-03-11).

Rollback checklist (short):
1) Pause canary traffic in routing plane (console -> rollout -> pause)
2) Promote previous artifact tag (promote artifact: release/2026.02-2026.03-stable)
3) Trigger cache invalidation on prefix caches (invalidate /kv/* where applicable)
4) Open rollback incident REL-ROLL-<timestamp> and notify on-call SRE + product (pager + slack)
5) Trigger post-rollback smoke tests and synthetic prompt-eval run
Owner: documented in Confluence (linked_artifacts).

Changelog seeds for v2026.03 (to be curated):
- HP-2026-03-05-A: tokenization fallback fix — reduces 502s on long instructions (PR #1287).
- HP-2026-03-08-B: kv-cache leak patch — prevents OOM in high-concurrency cases (PR #1299).
- Feature: Add API header X-Model-Variant to surface runtime variant for debugging (PR #1278) — experimental canary only.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Should we require CHANGES entries for very small config-only hotpatches? (ops preference: yes, always record).
- Is it feasible to run the 50-prompt model-quality checks without adding >15% latency to canary step? Lina to report perf delta.
- How to better surface changelog delta to Hosted API customers who use self-serve keys vs. enterprise customers with SLAs? Ruth to propose two-tier communication plan.

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal)
- Consider a hotpatch-staging channel that auto-creates a PR checklist item for CHANGES entry. Could be a git hook or GitHub Action.
- Keep a short "customer-facing delta" summary for every train (single paragraph) — put in release notes header.
- For Dedicated pinned customers, include a separate binary patch path (air-gapped) and track patch IDs in the changelog.

Next meeting: informal check on progress 2026-03-12 13:00 UTC; formal post-cut review scheduled 2026-03-14 16:00 UTC (post-mortem if anything >P1).

Attachments / quick links (for sprints):
- Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/loads/release-v2026.03
- Canary logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/q=canary%20v2026.03
- Automation ticket: REL-491 (TBD)

End of notes.
